insight.title: Why You Keep Finding Problems When Things Go Well
insight.subtitle: How your brain invents new issues as soon as you solve the old ones

sections.text: When a neighborhood becomes safer, residents often report more "suspicious" activity. Your brain doesn’t relax when problems disappear; it simply lowers the threshold for what it considers a problem to keep itself busy.
In a famous study, people shown blue dots eventually labeled purple dots as "blue" once the actual blue dots vanished. Your mind is wired to maintain a steady level of concern, regardless of reality.
This explains why a minor typo feels like a disaster on a quiet day. If you don't recognize this pattern, you will spend your life fixing imaginary issues that don’t actually matter.
Try this today: The next time you find a minor flaw today, ask if it actually matters.
High standards are useful, but hunting for ghosts is an expensive use of your attention.

news.title: Donald Trump plans major step against Iran… prepares to block Strait of Malacca after Hormuz, will US’ plan benefit India?
news.description: The United States is stepping up surveillance of the Strait of Malacca, a vital route to global trade and Asia's economy, following a new defense agreement with Indonesia.
news.why: Overseas online orders will take longer to reach your doorstep.

news.title: China's yuan dips after weak trade data, firming trend seen intact
news.description: China's yuan weakened slightly against the dollar on Wednesday after data showed a sharp slowdown in the country's March exports as the Iran war boosted energy costs and hurt global demand. ...
news.why: Slowing trade limits the variety of imported electronics on store shelves.

news.title: Ex-US Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen Says One Fed Rate Cut Possible This Year
news.description: The Former US Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen sees one interest rate cut by the Federal Reserve as possible this year, even as the Iran war creates supply shocks in the global economy that put pressure on inflation.
news.why: High interest rates keep your monthly mortgage and car payments expensive.

news.title: India's wholesale inflation rises to 3.88% in March as energy and manufacturing costs climb
news.description: The annual rate of inflation based on the All India Wholesale Price Index (WPI) reached 3.88 per cent for the month of March 2026, according to the latest data released by the government.
news.why: Rising manufacturing costs are pushing up the price of your groceries.

news.title: Small business outlook tumbles amid Iran war
news.description: Sentiment among U.S. small business owners dropped in March to the lowest level in nearly a year as the war with Iran pushed up energy costs and stoked economic uncertainty.
news.why: Local businesses are reducing their hours and cutting back on services.

news.title: BPCL, HPCL, IOC shares jump up to 5% as oil's skyrocketing rally cools down on fresh Iran-US peace talk hopes
news.description: OMC stocks surged as easing oil prices, driven by renewed hopes of US-Iran peace talks, lifted sentiment. Crude remained below the key $100 mark, reducing margin pressure concerns. Improved geopolitical outlook and steady vessel movement through Hormuz supported gains, while refiners also traded higher amid broader optimism in energy markets.
news.why: Falling oil prices are making your daily commute and travel cheaper.

news.title: OpenAI unveils GPT-5.4-Cyber a week after rival’s announcement of AI model
news.description: OpenAI has unveiled GPT-5.4-Cyber, a specialized model for defensive cybersecurity work. This comes after Anthropic’s announcement of their AI model Mythos, which has already identified thousands of vulnerabilities in software. GPT-5.4-Cyber will be initially rolled out to vetted security vendors, organizations, and researchers, with plans to expand the program to thousands of verified defenders.
news.why: New AI tools block hackers from accessing your private digital accounts.

news.title: Over 100 Chrome extensions caught stealing Google and Telegram data: How to stay safe?
news.description: Cybersecurity experts have reported a coordinated attack involving 108 Google Chrome extensions that steal user data and hijack Telegram sessions. Researchers say these extensions have been installed approximately 20,000 times
news.why: Malicious browser extensions put your private passwords and bank details at risk.

news.title: Maryland severs vaccine ties with CDC policies
news.description: As of July 1, a new law will allow the state of Maryland to determine what vaccines can be administered to individuals at least seven years of age, while also reducing certain out-of-pocket costs for families. news.why: Your state may change which vaccines are available at your local clinic.

news.title: NASA prepares to ship key rocket phase for Artemis III from New Orleans
news.description: Just a few days after Artemis II was completed, NASA announced plans for the next phase in its plan to return to the Moon.
news.why: These milestones drive technological breakthroughs that eventually sharpen your phone’s GPS.

news.title: Voltavate's Manufacturing Breakthrough Gains ARENA Backing to Transform Battery Production at Scale
news.description: Melbourne [Australia], April 15: Voltavate has been awarded $3.55 million in grant funding from the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA) to advance a new approach to battery manufacturing and accelerate its transition from laboratory development into pilot-scale production.
news.why: Future electric vehicles will travel much further on a single charge.
